q: How much coal does a 10 TPD tunnel kiln save over downdraft firing for refractories?
title: 10 TPD tunnel kiln vs downdraft: coal saved
short: It roughly halves coal per tonne fired. BEE's Godavari report puts downdraft kilns at 1.5 t of coal per tonne of refractories and a 10 TPD tunnel kiln at 0.78, saving 646 t of coal and about 1,137 t CO2 a year. Cost Rs 91 lakh, payback 3.30 years at 2011 prices.
audience: Refractory makers with steady orders weighing a tunnel kiln against their downdraft kilns

sections.h: Why downdraft kilns burn so much
p: A downdraft kiln heats its walls and the whole setting from cold every 8 to 10 days, then lets the heat go in cooling. The report measured 10 to 15% efficiency. A tunnel kiln fires continuously: ware is preheated by outgoing gas and cools inside the kiln, and the report assumes 35% efficiency.

ul: Downdraft: 45 t of 4,200 kcal/kg coal to fire 30 t of refractories, 1.5 t of coal per tonne.
Tunnel kiln: 1,150 kcal of heat per kg of product at 35% efficiency, 7.82 t of coal a day for 10 t, about 23.47 t for the same 30 t.
Saving 21.53 t a batch, 646 t a year over 30 batches, and Rs 27.57 lakh a year after Rs 1.50 lakh of extra power.
48 hours cool to cool; 24 hours from ambient to 1,200 C, 6 hours soaking at 1,000 C, 18 hours cooling.
Project cost Rs 91 lakh with civil and erection work included.

sections.h: When a tunnel kiln makes sense
ul: It only earns its saving running full: 10 t a day, every day, about 300 t a month of similar shapes.
35% efficiency is a design figure. Ask the supplier to guarantee kcal per kg fired.
Log coal and output for several months on the old kilns first, so the before figure is yours.

example.title: Per tonne fired and per year
lines: Downdraft: 1.50 t coal x 1.76 = 2.64 t CO2 per tonne of refractories
Tunnel kiln: 0.78 t coal x 1.76 = 1.37 t CO2 per tonne
Year: 646 t coal saved x 1.76 = 1,137 t CO2
The report's 1,162 t used 1.8 t CO2 per tonne of coal
example.note: Coal at our Indian coal factor, an estimate. The tunnel kiln's extra fan power is costed in the report but not given in kWh, so it is left out.

senseible: Senseible reads coal and electricity invoices into monthly CO2 records linked to each bill. Add tonnes fired and you have coal and CO2 per tonne, the before and after a lender wants for a kiln loan.
